title: LinuxCommandInventoryEntry
description: Authoritative upstream inventory record for an individual Linux executable utility.

command.description: Exact binary executable name as invoked in shell (e.g., 'sftp', 'ls', 'find', 'ip').

article_filename.description: Target repository path, strictly conforming to 'article/linux-<command>-tutorial.md'.

upstream_suite.description: Canonical upstream project or suite responsible for the utility.

upstream_package.description: Name of the upstream distribution package or source tree (e.g., 'coreutils', 'procps-ng').

upstream_homepage.description: Official canonical URL of the project home.

primary_url.description: Canonical online reference maintained by the project (e.g., man.openbsd.org, gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual).

source_repo_url.description: Direct link to upstream repository manual source (e.g., git repo .adoc, .1, or .texi file).

is_posix_standardized.description: True if specified in IEEE Std 1003.1-2024 (POSIX.1-2024) Shell and Utilities.

posix_url.description: Canonical link to The Open Group POSIX.1-2024 utility specification if standardized.

current_researched_version.description: Exact upstream release version researched (e.g., 'OpenSSH 10.5', 'GNU Coreutils 9.11', 'rsync 3.5.0').

research_date.description: ISO-8601 calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) when authoritative upstream documentation was audited.

lifecycle_status.description: Upstream maintenance lifecycle status. Obsolete utilities (e.g., procps-ng skill/snice) must be documented as obsolete.

execution_safety_tier.description: Safety level determining testing isolation requirements during article verification.

collision_resolution.description: Details handling when multiple upstream projects ship an executable of the same name (e.g., 'uptime', 'kill', 'echo').

kernel_dependency.description: Explicit kernel subsystem or minimum version required for full utility capability (critical for iproute2, util-linux namespaces, bpf).
